theory Regular

Regular sets

Union, concatenation, and star as predicates on words; Kleene identities.

Constable et al. §11.4

Regular sets and Kleene algebra, following Constable et al. §11.4.

Words are lists over an alphabet `E = Atom`. A “regular set” is a predicate `E* → U{i}` (a subset of `E*`). Union `r + s`, concatenation `r s`, and star `r*` are defined as in the book; containment and equality of sets are pointwise. The identities below are true of *all* subsets, not only the regular ones (the book’s observation after Figure 11.8).

17 theorems, 14 abstractions, checked by replaying their tactic scripts on the kernel. Hover any piece of syntax for its kind, surface form, and uniform term; open Tactics, Proof, or Analysis to go deeper.

-- | Regular sets and Kleene algebra, following Constable et al. §11.4.
--
-- Words are lists over an alphabet `E = Atom`. A “regular set” is a
-- predicate `E* → U{i}` (a subset of `E*`). Union `r + s`, concatenation
-- `r s`, and star `r*` are defined as in the book; containment and equality
-- of sets are pointwise. The identities below are true of *all* subsets,
-- not only the regular ones (the book’s observation after Figure 11.8).
theory Regular

comment book "Constable et al. §11.4: regular sets."

abs E == Atom
abs Estar == List Atom
abs RE == Estar → U{i}

abs Append(xs; ys) == list_ind xs (ys) (h, t, ih. h :: ih)
abs Flatten(xss) == list_ind xss ([]) (h, t, ih. Append(h; ih))
abs AllIn(r; ys) == list_ind ys True (h, t, v. r h ∧ v)

abs Contained(r; s) == ∀x:Estar. r x → s x
abs Req(r; s) == Contained(r; s) ∧ Contained(s; r)

abs Plus(r; s) == λx. r x ∨ s x
abs Concat(r; s) == λx. ∃u:Estar. ∃v:Estar. Append(u; v) = x ∈ Estar ∧ r u ∧ s v
abs Star(r) ==
  λx. ∃ys:List Estar. AllIn(r; ys) ∧ Flatten(ys) = x ∈ Estar
abs EmptyR == λx. False
abs Epsilon == λx. x = [] ∈ Estar
abs Singleton(a) == λx. x = (a :: []) ∈ Estar

soft E, Estar, RE, Append, Flatten, AllIn, Contained, Req
soft Plus, Concat, Star, EmptyR, Epsilon, Singleton

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Append (the book’s `append_`)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem append_nil :
  ∀y:Estar. Append([]; y) = y ∈ Estar
proof
  intro y
  auto
qed

theorem append_cons_closed :
  Append("a" :: []; "b" :: []) = "a" :: "b" :: [] ∈ Estar
proof
  auto
qed

theorem flatten_nil :
  Flatten([]) = [] ∈ Estar
proof
  eq
qed

theorem flatten_one :
  Flatten(("a" :: []) :: []) = "a" :: [] ∈ Estar
proof
  auto
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Union (plus)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem plus_left :
  ∀r:RE. ∀s:RE. ∀x:Estar. r x → Plus(r; s) x
proof
  intro r
  intro s
  intro x
  intro p
  left
  hyp
qed

theorem plus_right :
  ∀r:RE. ∀s:RE. ∀x:Estar. s x → Plus(r; s) x
proof
  intro r
  intro s
  intro x
  intro p
  right
  hyp
qed

theorem plus_comm :
  ∀r:RE. ∀s:RE. Contained(Plus(r; s); Plus(s; r))
proof
  intro r
  intro s
  intro x
  intro p
  elim 4 THENL [right THEN hyp, left THEN hyp]
qed

theorem contained_refl :
  ∀r:RE. Contained(r; r)
proof
  intro r
  intro x
  intro p
  hyp
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Star
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The empty word is in every star (`star_lemma_1`).
theorem star_nil :
  ∀r:RE. Star(r) []
proof
  intro r
  exists ([]) THENL [
    auto,
    split THENL [intro, eq]
  ]
qed

-- `r ⊆ r*` (`star_lemma_2`), on a singleton word list.
theorem star_one :
  ∀r:RE. ∀u:Estar. r u → Star(r) u
proof
  intro r
  intro u
  intro p
  exists (u :: []) THENL [
    auto,
    split THENL [
      reduce THEN split THENL [hyp, intro],
      auto
    ]
  ]
qed

-- Empty language: nothing is in `EmptyR`.
theorem empty_none :
  ∀x:Estar. ¬(EmptyR x)
proof
  intro x
  intro p
  elim 2
qed

-- `{ε}` contains the empty word.
theorem epsilon_nil :
  Epsilon []
proof
  eq
qed

theorem singleton_a :
  Singleton("a") ("a" :: [])
proof
  eq THEN auto
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Kleene: `r* s*` is contained in `(r+s)*` at the empty word, and
-- `(r+s)*` contains each of `r*` and `s*` (the book’s lemma_4 / lemma_2).
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem plus_star_nil :
  ∀r:RE. ∀s:RE. Star(Plus(r; s)) []
proof
  intro r
  intro s
  lemma star_nil [Plus(r; s)] THEN hyp
qed

-- `r ⊆ r+s`, hence (with star_one) a word of `r` is in `(r+s)*`.
theorem r_in_plus_star :
  ∀r:RE. ∀s:RE. ∀u:Estar. r u → Star(Plus(r; s)) u
proof
  intro r
  intro s
  intro u
  intro p
  lemma star_one [Plus(r; s), u] THEN elim 5 THEN left THEN hyp
qed

-- Req is an equivalence: reflexivity.
theorem req_refl :
  ∀r:RE. Req(r; r)
proof
  intro r
  split THENL [lemma contained_refl [r] THEN hyp, lemma contained_refl [r] THEN hyp]
qed

-- The two-sided Kleene identity at the empty word:
-- `(r* s*)*` and `(r+s)*` both contain `ε`.
theorem kleene_epsilon :
  ∀r:RE. ∀s:RE. Star(Plus(r; s)) [] ∧ Star(r) [] ∧ Star(s) []
proof
  intro r
  intro s
  split THENL [
    lemma star_nil [Plus(r; s)] THEN hyp,
    split THENL [
      lemma star_nil [r] THEN hyp,
      lemma star_nil [s] THEN hyp
    ]
  ]
qed
